A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MACE-TNP study. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C support reliable comparison. The additional pages in v2 contain a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original synthetic-data experiments, architectural ablations, and evaluation on the Sachs proteomics dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix C, including synthetic evaluations, ablations, and Sachs results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same variable-specific embeddings, alternating sample/node attention, Gaussian-mixture decoder, training objective, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two-node models, three-node confounder/mediator and GP/NN settings, distribution shifts, higher-dimensional synthetic systems, and Sachs dataset. No task or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DiBS-GP, ARCO-GP, BCI-GPN, DECI, and NOGAM+GP. Tables 2 and 5 retain their original comparator sets, which exclude BCI-GPN.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B-C retain the data-generation procedures, training budgets, model configurations, default 500-observation/500-intervention testing protocol, and KL/NLPID metrics. The checklist does not introduce new evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same confounder/mediator analysis, interventional-sample sensitivity experiments, GP/NN distribution-shift tests, and attention, mixture-component, and model-size ablations in Appendix C.

E5.justification: Mean-error reporting, Figure 3's medians and 10-90% quantiles, and the Monte Carlo KL-estimation procedure remain unchanged. The new checklist restates existing uncertainty-reporting practices without adding run counts or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: All matched table entries and plotted findings are retained. For example, Table 1 reports MACE-TNP NLPID of 563.9 ± 23.4 on GP data and 527.9 ± 19.8 on NN data in both versions; Table 5 retains 998.9 ± 104.9 on Sachs.

T1.justification: The definitions, mathematical objectives, Lemma 1, Theorems B.1-B.2, and appendix proofs are unchanged. Section 4 changes the Bruinsma proposition reference from 3.26 to 3.34 and adjusts attribution without changing the mathematical assertion.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: amortized Bayesian interventional estimation, empirical recovery of tractable posteriors, and competitive or superior results across increasingly complex settings.

C2.justification: Interpretations of identifiability, implicit adjustment, and distribution-shift performance remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations concerning training resources, prior coverage, and quadratic attention costs; the checklist adds no substantive scientific qualification.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly provides an experiment-code repository link. The checklist also states that supplementary code includes synthetic-data generation and model implementation. Existing hyperparameters, hardware specifications, and training-time disclosures in Appendix C.1 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 now explicitly credits Gordon et al. [25] alongside Bruinsma for exact prediction-map recovery. This is a limited attribution refinement involving an already-cited work; the related-work discussion and bibliography remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a standardized NeurIPS checklist between the references and appendices, updates the publication footer, and makes limited citation and cross-reference edits. The research narrative and organization of the scientific sections remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Title-page spacing and some text and figure positions change slightly, and checklist pages are inserted. The seven figures and five tables retain their content, captions, and display structure; appendix pagination shifts without a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The explicit code location in Section 5 improves implementation discoverability and reproducibility documentation, while the revised attribution improves traceability of the recovery claim. The scientific evidence is unchanged, and the checklist largely repeats existing information, so the overall benefit is limited. Repository completeness cannot be established from the PDFs.
